title: How Salary Packaging HECS Affects Your Hourly to Annual Pay Conversion
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay with a 38-hour week, and understand salary packaging HECS, tax, super, and casual loading. Australian guide.
salarySummary: Assuming a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year.

faqs.q: How does salary packaging HECS affect my hourly to annual conversion?
faqs.a: Salary packaging HECS (Higher Education Loan Program) allows you to reduce your taxable income by packaging certain items, but it does not change your gross hourly rate. The annual pay calculation remains hourly × hours × 52, but your tax and HELP repayment may be adjusted. Consult your employer or tax advisor.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the base rate set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are industry-specific minimums that may be higher. Casual employees also receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on hourly pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your hourly rate. For a 38-hour week, super is calculated on your gross ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you're paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual pay is essential. This guide explains the conversion, the role of the 38-hour week, and how factors like casual loading, superannuation, and **salary packaging HECS** affect your take-home pay. We'll also cover the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and the difference between ordinary-time earnings and total earnings.

## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

### The Basic Formula

The standard method to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It's a starting point for comparing offers or budgeting.

### Why 38 Hours?

In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. When using our [timesheet](/), we assume 38 hours unless you adjust the hours. For part-time or casual workers, your actual weekly hours may differ, so adjust accordingly.

### Example: National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour. For a 38-hour week:

- Weekly pay: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Annual pay: $1,004.90 × 52 = $52,254.80

This is the minimum for a full-time adult employee not covered by an award. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour.

## Understanding Different Pay Rates

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are industry-specific minimums that are often higher. For example, the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides details on current rates. Always check your award or enterprise agreement for your correct rate.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are paid a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave and other entitlements. When using our timesheet, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. **Do not** type a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool adds it automatically.

## Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, at the minimum wage:

- Fortnightly: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80

This helps with budgeting and comparing salary offers that are quoted per fortnight.

## Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax scale for 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (generally). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help estimate net income.

## Superannuation

Superannuation Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. For a full-time worker earning $52,254.80, the employer contributes an extra $6,270.58 per year (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). This is not deducted from your pay – it's additional. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

## Salary Packaging HECS

**Salary packaging HECS** refers to arranging your salary to reduce taxable income, which can affect your HELP (Higher Education Loan Program) repayment obligations. While salary packaging does not change your gross hourly rate or the annual conversion formula, it can lower your assessable income, potentially reducing tax and HELP repayments. However, this guide does not model salary packaging – it's an estimate only. Consult a tax professional or your employer for advice.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page where you type your base hourly rate. The tool calculates annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly pay based on 38 hours. You can adjust hours if needed. The casual loading checkbox adds 25% on top of the base rate. Remember: the annual figure is an estimate, not a determination of your pay.

## Key Distinctions

- **Ordinary-time earnings** are the base pay for standard hours. This is what super is calculated on.
- **Total earnings** include overtime, bonuses, and allowances. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 (May 2026), and for all employees (including part-time) at $1,579.20. These are averages, not medians for a specific job.
- **Casual loading** is additional pay, not part of ordinary-time earnings for super purposes.

## Conclusion

Converting hourly to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. But remember to consider your actual hours, award rate, casual loading, super, and tax. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page for more examples. For salary packaging HECS, seek tailored advice. This guide provides a starting point for your pay calculations.
